gaps.sentence: Even after she moved abroad, we ___ in touch by email.
gaps.explanation: keep in touch means to maintain contact with someone.

gaps.sentence: It took him months to ___ the habit of biting his nails.
gaps.explanation: break a habit (or kick a habit) means to stop doing something you do regularly.

gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: Their wedding ___ place on a remote island.
gaps.explanation: 'Take place' is the fixed phrase for events.

gaps.sentence: Who will ___ responsibility for the project now that Jane has left?
gaps.explanation: take responsibility for something means to accept the duty of dealing with it.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: Local residents are deeply ___ about the new motorway plan.
gaps.explanation: deeply concerned is the standard collocation meaning very worried; the other adjectives do not collocate with 'deeply'.

gaps.sentence: I only ___ sight of the celebrity for a second before the crowd closed in.
gaps.explanation: catch sight of somebody/something means to notice them briefly.
